newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ dlr takes brunt of easing momentum after data.
newsitem.headline: NZ dlr takes brunt of easing momentum after data.

text.p: The New Zealand dollar slipped around 15 basis points in late Tuesday morning trade following employment data that confirmed a picture of a soft economy.
By midday the kiwi was at US0.6865/72, down from 0.6880/87 just before Statistics New Zealand (SNZ) said at 10.45 a.m. that employment growth fell 0.1 percent in the March quarter.
SNZ said the unemployment rate rose to 6.4 percent from 5.9 percent in the previous quarter.
The key 90-day bank bill rate initially blipped down to 6.69 percent from 6.74 percent just before the data, but by midday had bounced back up to 6.73 percent.
Meanwhile the currency's Trade-Weighted Index was down at 68.23 from 68.45 before the announcement.

Dealers said the market was picking that Reserve Bank governor Don Brash could live with easier monetary conditions, but that easing looked set to come more through the currency rather than short term interest rates.
